title: Protection that works
summary: Lock everything but the inputs, hide formulas you don’t want edited, let people sort and filter, give different people different cells, and know what protection can’t do.
objectives: Unlock the input cells and protect the sheet, choosing what people may still do.
Hide formulas from the formula bar, and protect the workbook’s structure.
Use Allow Edit Ranges to give different people different cells.
Avoid the gotchas: Tables on protected sheets, sorting and filtering, and protection that isn’t security.

p: Every cell starts Locked, but Locked does nothing until the sheet is protected. So unlock the inputs first, then protect the sheet.
Select the inputs (B3:B10), Ctrl+1 › Protection › untick Locked.
Home › Find & Select › Go To Special › Constants selects every typed value: a quick way to find inputs.
Locking doesn’t change how a cell looks, which is why inputs get a colour.
In real life: found a supervisor had typed 54000 over the order value formula. Every request after that showed ₹54,000.

p: Tick Hidden as well as Locked, and once the sheet is protected the formula bar shows nothing for that cell. The result still shows in the cell.
Use it to keep the formula bar uncluttered for users.
It isn’t secrecy: anyone with a copy of the file can get the formulas back.
Leave formulas visible on sheets other analysts must check.
In real life: hides the discount formula, so the sales team quote from the result instead of arguing with the formula.

p: Protect Sheet lists what users may still do on a protected sheet. The defaults allow only selecting cells; tick what your users really need.
Use AutoFilter: people can filter, but only if the filter arrows are on before you protect.
Sort: works only on ranges whose cells are unlocked.
Insert rows: new rows are locked like the rows around them.
In real life: ticked Use AutoFilter on the order log. The team filter by supplier every morning without asking her to unprotect it.

p: Allow Edit Ranges gives a range its own password. Stores can change quantities; only Farah, with her password, can change the approval limit.
Review › Allow Edit Ranges › New: a title, the cells, a range password.
Then Protect Sheet: the ranges only work on a protected sheet.
Unlocked cells stay open to everyone; ranges are for cells that need a password.
In real life: keeps the approval limit and supplier prices in a range only she can open. Everyone else fills in requests as before.

p: Protection changes how some features behave. Know these before your users find them.
Test the protected sheet as a user before you share it.
Unprotect, change, protect again: keep the password with the workbook’s owner.
In real life: stopped growing the day he protected it. New rows missed the formulas until he moved the log to its own unprotected sheet.

What to do

the range has locked cells: unlock the data cells

p: Protect Workbook locks the structure: nobody can add, delete, rename, hide or unhide sheets. A password to open the file is the only one that keeps people out.
Hide the Lists sheet, then protect the structure so it can’t be unhidden.
Sheet and structure passwords stop accidents, not people who are determined: free tools remove them.
Keep confidential data out of the file, or encrypt it and share it with the right people only.
In real life: never puts salaries in a workbook protected only by a sheet password. Payroll files are encrypted and shared with two people.

lab.intro: The purchase request form is finished. Practise the protection steps here, then do it for real in Excel with the Module 1 lab below.

cells.A2: Type in the green cells only. The yellow cells work themselves out.

tasks.prompt: Select the cells Ganesh’s team must be able to **type in**, ready to unlock them.
hints: From the request date to the needed-by date.
tasks.msg: Select the green inputs, B3:B10: those are the cells to unlock.

tasks.prompt: In Format Cells, click the setting that hides a cell’s **formula** from the formula bar once the sheet is protected.
In Protect Sheet, click the option that lets people **filter** the protected sheet.
hints: Filtering uses the arrows in the header row.
It’s near the bottom of the list.

tasks.prompt: Put the steps in order to give Farah her own password for the approval limit in E4.
hints: Protection last: ranges only work on a protected sheet.
Test as a user at the end.
items: Title: Approval limit; Refers to cells: =$E$4
Type a range password and confirm it
Try to change E4: Excel asks for the password

tasks.prompt: Ganesh’s request log is an Excel Table on a protected sheet. He types a new request in the row below the Table. What happens?
hints: Think about what a Table normally does with a new row.
tasks.explain: A Table can’t resize on a protected sheet. Keep logs on an unprotected sheet, or size the Table in advance.
options: The Table doesn’t grow, so the new row misses its formulas and formatting

why.0: That’s what happens on an unprotected sheet.

tasks.prompt: A price list goes to the wrong customer by email. Which protection would have kept them out?
hints: Most protection only works inside the file.
tasks.explain: Only encryption stops someone opening the file. The others prevent accidental changes once it’s open.

why.0: They can still open it and read every value.
why.2: That stops changes to the sheets, not reading them.

real.title: Make the purchase request form safe
steps: Download the starter file: the purchase request form, and a **Lists** sheet with a name, **Departments**.
Click **B5**. Data › Data Validation › Allow **List**, Source **=Departments**.
Click **B8**. Allow **Whole number**, between **1** and **5000**. On the Input Message tab: “Pairs or pieces, 1 to 5,000.”
Click **B10**. Allow **Date**, Data **greater than or equal to**, Start date **=B3**. Error Alert: Stop, “The needed-by date can’t be before the request date.”
Review › **Protect Sheet** (no password needed for this lab). Check: B8 accepts 600; B12 refuses typing. Save and upload.

quiz.q: What does the Locked setting do on an unprotected sheet?
quiz.explain: It only matters once the sheet is protected.

quiz.q: You tick Hidden on B12 and protect the sheet. What do users see?
options: The value in the cell, but no formula in the formula bar

quiz.q: Sort is ticked in Protect Sheet, but sorting is refused. Why?
options: Sort never works on protected sheets
quiz.explain: Unlock the data cells you want sorted.
Protect the sheet after setting the ranges.

quiz.q: Which stops sheets being deleted or renamed?
Is a sheet password real security?
options: No: it prevents accidents; free tools remove it

points: Unlock the inputs (Ctrl+1 › Protection), then **Protect Sheet**, ticking what users may still do (**Use AutoFilter**, **Sort**).
**Hidden** keeps formulas out of the formula bar; **Allow Edit Ranges** gives ranges their own passwords; **Protect Workbook** locks the sheets.
Gotchas: Tables don’t grow on protected sheets; sorting needs unlocked cells; sheet passwords aren’t security.
recap.cheat: Unlock inputs, protect the sheet, allow only what users need; encrypt the file to keep people out.
